title: Promissory estoppel
summary: Promissory estoppel can make a promise binding when it foreseeably induces action or forbearance and enforcement is necessary to avoid injustice. The remedy may be limited as justice requires.
notes:
Identify the promise, the action it was expected to induce, the action actually taken, and the resulting injustice if the promise is left unenforced. Ricketts concerns leaving employment; Feinberg concerns retirement; D&G Stout concerns rejecting a business-sale opportunity. Drennan uses reliance to protect an opportunity to accept a subcontractor’s bid. These are different applications with different remedial consequences. The casebook reproduces both Restatement formulations of § 90; preserve the distinction between their wording and between enforcement of a promise and recovery of a particular amount.

The materials develop reliance-based enforcement from Ricketts through two versions of § 90, Feinberg, Cohen, D&G Stout, and Drennan. A promise, induced reliance, and the injustice inquiry perform distinct work. D&G Stout does not promise future profits for an indefinite period; Drennan protects a chance to accept an offer. Relief may be limited as justice requires under the second Restatement wording. Case-specific holdings and jurisdictional formulations should remain separate.
